anomalies.observed: Two electrically unrelated nets are exported under the identical auto-name NET0108: net code 99 groups the Ethernet common-mode / input-bridge AC node (C16 pin1, D32 pin4, JP9 pin2, TR2 pin21), while net code 144 groups the USB data line (Module2 pin103 USB2_N, U8 pin6 D-). A KiCad netlist reader matches nets by name, so these two entries collapse into one copper net.
anomalies.expected: USB2_N / USB D- must be its own net, separate from the Ethernet magnetics common-mode node and the rectifier AC input; auto-generated NETxxxx names are unique per net in a correct export.
anomalies.impact: The CM4 USB D- line (and the host-port mux U8 D-) would be shorted to the Ethernet transformer center-tap/common-mode node and the AC input of the input bridge rectifier. USB would not enumerate and the Ethernet front-end common-mode node would be loaded by the USB PHY, breaking both interfaces.

anomalies.observed: R100's schematic value is '24k' (and the SPICE deck uses 24k), but its MPN field is 'FRC0805J240TSD' and its description states '24Ω', i.e. the orderable part is 24 Ω, three orders of magnitude lower than the schematic value.
anomalies.expected: The MPN/description should agree with the schematic value (24k bleeder across the rectified motor rail); a 24 Ω part across VOUTP/VOUTN would dissipate far more than an 0805 125 mW resistor can handle.
anomalies.impact: If assembled from the MPN/description, a 24 Ω resistor is placed as the VOUTP-VOUTN bleeder instead of 24 kΩ, overloading the motor power rail and burning the part.
